notes: All 153 pages read end to end: the project description and methodology, the citywide development narrative, the three period chapters (1865-1905, 1906-1929, 1930-1965) with their storefront-component sections and evaluative frameworks, the signage chapter, the 1970s-2000s trends chapter, the preservation recommendations and the bibliography. It is a citywide thematic statement with no appendix inventory, no APNs and no per-property status codes: its address-level yield is the buildings it names as type examples, as worked examples in the integrity evaluations, and in the landmark-designation recommendations. Nearly every one of those comes with a build year, an architect or builder, a style, or all three. Its three maps count the surviving stock (about 2,000 pre-1906 buildings, 4,220 from 1906-1929 and 1,542 from 1930-1965 in the commercial zoning districts) but name none of them.
